$comment: Registry of the webview panels the visual harness renders.
Each entry mirrors one panel's HTML shell in vscode-extension/src/extension.ts:
bundle  — the esbuild entry point name in esbuild.js (dist/webview/<bundle>.js)
global  — the window global that shell assigns the view's data to
globals — optional additional globals the panel shell sets before its bundle
fixture — a JSON file in ./fixtures holding that data
To add a view: add its esbuild entry point name here, capture the data its
shell passes (the __INITIAL_*__ payload) into a fixture, and run
`node render-views.js --view <id>` to check it renders.
scenarios: optional scripted click/select flows replayed by
scripts/interaction-smoke.js. The one-pass control crawl cannot change a
<select> or reach a control that only appears after another one was used,
so a view declares those flows here: each step is a `click` or a `select`
(with an optional `value`; otherwise the next enabled option is taken), and
`expect` is a selector the view must still be showing after every step. A step
may also declare `expectPosted`: the command it must post to the host (which
must have a host handler), so a click whose listener is missing fails.
states: optional per-view list of the tabs and modes the visual diff also
screenshots. A view is otherwise captured only in its initial render, so a
change on any other tab diffs as 'unchanged'. Each state has an `id` (the
screenshot is <view>--<id>.<theme>.png), a `title`, `steps` in the same
click/select/post format as scenarios (replayed on a fresh page; `post`
delivers a host message for a tab that loads its content on open), and an
`expect` selector that must be showing afterwards, or the render is an
error. Optional `settleMs` overrides the wait after the steps (a tab that
lazily loads Chart.js and animates in needs more than the default), and
optional `noiseFloorPixels` gives a canvas-drawing state its own tolerance.
noiseFloorPixels: how many differing pixels count as run-to-run noise
rather than a real change. Only views that draw to a <canvas> need it —
anti-aliasing there is not perfectly reproducible. Omit it (default 0) so
DOM-rendered views are compared exactly.

scenarios.name: Clicking a By Editor card filters the charts to it; clicking it again clears the filter
Install, link and sync buttons post their messages
Score/Toolbox switch swaps the panel and the copy action follows it

views.title: Usage Analysis
$statesComment: Every tab of the usage panel; 'activity' is the initial render. The
Workspace, GitHub and Coaching leaf bars stay hidden until their group tab
is clicked, so those states click the group first — the same two-step shape
the diagnostics states below use. A state that clicks straight at a hidden
leaf button fails to render at all, which takes the visual diff, the CI
screenshots and the release video's shot of that tab down with it.

scenarios.name: Tools tab: repository memories Ask Copilot and Open file buttons
$comment: The one-pass crawl only clicks the initial tab, so it never reaches these
buttons. Ask Copilot posts draftServerMemoryPromotion (the host re-probes the
target and drafts, never submits); Open file posts openServerMemoryCitation for a documented
memory's cited file. expectPosted fails the step if the message is not sent.

stages.name: Standardized software delivery
stages.summary: Automated builds, tests that run on every change, dependency updates and a protected main branch. Nothing above this stage is trustworthy without it.

stages.name: AI-assisted engineers
stages.summary: Developers remain the authors. Repository-level instructions steer assistants; AI policy and telemetry boundaries are written down.

stages.name: Agent-delegated, human-reviewed
stages.summary: Small bounded work packages with strong review discipline. An agent may branch, implement, test and open a pull request, but cannot approve or merge its own work.

stages.name: Spec-driven autonomous team
stages.summary: Versioned specifications, acceptance scenarios, independent evaluators, risk classification and progressive delivery. Humans approve intent and outcomes, not every line.

controls.label: CI workflows
controls.why: Automated delivery has to exist before anything can be delegated to an agent.
controls.remediation: Add at least one GitHub Actions workflow under .github/workflows/.

controls.label: Tests executed in CI
controls.why: A green build is only evidence when the build actually runs tests.
controls.remediation: Run the test suite from a workflow step so every change is validated.

controls.label: Automated dependency updates
controls.why: Supply-chain currency is part of reliable delivery, not an AI feature.
controls.remediation: Add .github/dependabot.yml, or a Renovate configuration (renovate.json).

controls.label: Reproducible environment
controls.why: A result transfers between agents and humans more reliably when both start from the same environment. Useful, but a repository can deliver reliably without one.
controls.remediation: Add a .devcontainer/ configuration, or a .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml for the coding agent.

controls.label: Infrastructure as code
controls.why: Environments that are clicked together by hand cannot be rebuilt or rolled back automatically. Only assessed when the workflows deploy to cloud infrastructure.
controls.remediation: Describe the environment in Terraform, Bicep, Pulumi, Helm or Kubernetes manifests.
controls.detail: No workflow deploys to cloud infrastructure, so this does not apply here.

controls.label: Code scanning
controls.why: Static analysis is one of the few automated checks that keeps meaning when a machine wrote the code.
controls.remediation: Enable CodeQL — either the default setup or a .github/workflows/codeql.yml workflow.
controls.unknownReason: CodeQL default setup leaves no file in the repository, so a missing workflow does not mean scanning is off.

controls.label: Branch protection or rulesets
controls.why: Without an enforced target branch, every control above it is advisory.
controls.remediation: Protect the default branch with a ruleset that requires status checks.
controls.detail: Needs a GitHub token with access to this repository — not checked.

controls.label: Repository instructions
controls.why: Assistants need the repository's own conventions written down, not inferred.
controls.remediation: Add .github/copilot-instructions.md.

controls.label: Agent instructions (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md)
controls.why: Cross-vendor agent instructions keep guidance in one place rather than per tool.
controls.remediation: Add AGENTS.md (and mirror it for other agents where needed).

controls.label: Path-scoped instructions
controls.why: A monolithic instruction file stops scaling once a repository has distinct subsystems.
controls.remediation: Add .github/instructions/*.instructions.md scoped with applyTo globs.

controls.label: AI usage policy and telemetry boundaries
controls.why: The paper is explicit that AI adoption needs a stated policy and telemetry boundaries, and that individual performance scoring is out of bounds.
controls.remediation: Write down the AI usage policy, what telemetry is collected, and that it is never used to score individuals.
controls.detail: A written policy or decision — not machine-detectable.

controls.label: Custom agents
controls.why: Bounded work packages need agents with a defined remit, not one general-purpose agent.
controls.remediation: Define agents under .github/agents/.

controls.label: Agent skills
controls.why: Repeatable procedures belong in a skill so every run does the same thing.
controls.remediation: Add .github/skills/<name>/SKILL.md for the procedures agents keep repeating.

controls.label: Declared MCP servers
controls.why: Tool access an agent is given has to be declared in the repository to be reviewable.
controls.remediation: Declare the MCP servers the repository's agents may use in .vscode/mcp.json or .mcp.json.

controls.label: Agent-authored pull requests
controls.why: Delegation is only real once agents are actually opening pull requests in this repository.
controls.remediation: Delegate a bounded work package to a coding agent and let it open a draft pull request.
controls.detail: Needs a GitHub token with access to this repository — not checked.

controls.label: Human review enforced on merge
controls.why: The stage-3 boundary is that an agent can propose but cannot approve or merge its own work.
controls.remediation: Require pull request reviews from someone other than the author on the protected branch.
controls.detail: Needs a GitHub token with access to this repository — not checked.

controls.label: Issue Forms as an intent queue
controls.why: Structured intent is what makes a work package specifiable rather than a paragraph of prose.
controls.remediation: Add .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml Issue Forms capturing intent, constraints and acceptance criteria.

controls.label: Versioned specifications
controls.why: Spec-driven work needs specifications that are reviewed and versioned like code.
controls.remediation: Keep specifications under specs/ or docs/specs/ in the repository.

controls.label: Executable acceptance scenarios
controls.why: Acceptance has to be executable for an evaluator to be independent of the implementer.
controls.remediation: Express acceptance scenarios as executable tests (for example .feature files or an acceptance test suite).

controls.label: Independent evaluator
controls.why: The agent that implements a change must not be the only judge of it. Copilot code review, another AI reviewer, or a separate review, test or security agent all count.
controls.remediation: Turn on Copilot code review for pull requests, or define a separate review, test or security agent under .github/agents/.
controls.unknownReason: Copilot code review turned on through a ruleset or organization policy leaves no file in the repository, so no evaluator found here does not mean there is none.
controls.detail: Copilot code review turned on through a ruleset or organization policy leaves no file in the repository, so no evaluator found here does not mean there is none.

controls.label: Agentic workflows
controls.why: Autonomy that runs on a schedule or an event has to be defined in the repository to be governed.
controls.remediation: Define agentic workflows in .github/workflows/ so their triggers and permissions are reviewable.

controls.label: Deployment environments declared
controls.why: Progressive delivery needs named environments before it can have gates.
controls.remediation: Declare `environment:` on the deploying job.
controls.unknownReason: Environments can be deployed to from a reusable workflow this scan cannot read.
controls.detail: No workflow deploys to cloud infrastructure, so this does not apply here.

controls.label: Environment protection rules
controls.why: A named environment without required reviewers or wait timers gates nothing.
controls.remediation: Add required reviewers or a wait timer to the production environment.
controls.detail: No workflow deploys to cloud infrastructure, so this does not apply here.

controls.label: Artifact attestations
controls.why: Once nobody reads every line, provenance is the evidence that the artefact you shipped is the one the governed pipeline built. It is a supply-chain control first, so it is recommended here rather than required.
controls.remediation: Use actions/attest-build-provenance in the release workflow.
controls.unknownReason: Attestations can be produced by workflows this scan cannot read, or by a shared reusable workflow.
controls.detail: Attestations can be produced by workflows this scan cannot read, or by a shared reusable workflow.

controls.label: Documented risk classification
controls.why: Autonomy is permitted per risk class, so the risk classes have to exist and be written down.
controls.remediation: Classify the repository's change types by risk and state which classes may be handled autonomously.
controls.detail: A written policy or decision — not machine-detectable.

findings.title: Workflows run with unbounded permissions
findings.detail: release.yml declare(s) `permissions: write-all`. Autonomy is only safe inside a pre-approved envelope — grant the least privilege each job needs.

controls.remediation: Enable CodeQL — either the default setup or a .github/workflows/codeql.yml workflow.
controls.unknownReason: CodeQL default setup leaves no file in the repository, so a missing workflow does not mean scanning is off.
controls.detail: A GitHub-specific check, and this repository's remote is not on GitHub — not checked.

controls.label: Branch protection or rulesets
controls.why: Without an enforced target branch, every control above it is advisory.
controls.remediation: Protect the default branch with a ruleset that requires status checks.
controls.detail: A GitHub-specific check, and this repository's remote is not on GitHub — not checked.

controls.label: Repository instructions
controls.why: Assistants need the repository's own conventions written down, not inferred.
controls.remediation: Add .github/copilot-instructions.md.

controls.label: Agent instructions (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md)
controls.why: Cross-vendor agent instructions keep guidance in one place rather than per tool.
controls.remediation: Add AGENTS.md (and mirror it for other agents where needed).

controls.label: Path-scoped instructions
controls.why: A monolithic instruction file stops scaling once a repository has distinct subsystems.
controls.remediation: Add .github/instructions/*.instructions.md scoped with applyTo globs.

controls.label: AI usage policy and telemetry boundaries
controls.why: The paper is explicit that AI adoption needs a stated policy and telemetry boundaries, and that individual performance scoring is out of bounds.
controls.remediation: Write down the AI usage policy, what telemetry is collected, and that it is never used to score individuals.
controls.detail: A written policy or decision — not machine-detectable.

controls.label: Custom agents
controls.why: Bounded work packages need agents with a defined remit, not one general-purpose agent.
controls.remediation: Define agents under .github/agents/.

controls.label: Agent skills
controls.why: Repeatable procedures belong in a skill so every run does the same thing.
controls.remediation: Add .github/skills/<name>/SKILL.md for the procedures agents keep repeating.

controls.label: Declared MCP servers
controls.why: Tool access an agent is given has to be declared in the repository to be reviewable.
controls.remediation: Declare the MCP servers the repository's agents may use in .vscode/mcp.json or .mcp.json.

controls.label: Agent-authored pull requests
controls.why: Delegation is only real once agents are actually opening pull requests in this repository.
controls.remediation: Delegate a bounded work package to a coding agent and let it open a draft pull request.
controls.detail: A GitHub-specific check, and this repository's remote is not on GitHub — not checked.

controls.label: Human review enforced on merge
controls.why: The stage-3 boundary is that an agent can propose but cannot approve or merge its own work.
controls.remediation: Require pull request reviews from someone other than the author on the protected branch.
controls.detail: A GitHub-specific check, and this repository's remote is not on GitHub — not checked.

controls.label: Issue Forms as an intent queue
controls.why: Structured intent is what makes a work package specifiable rather than a paragraph of prose.
controls.remediation: Add .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml Issue Forms capturing intent, constraints and acceptance criteria.
controls.detail: A GitHub-specific check, and this repository's remote is not on GitHub — not checked.

controls.label: Versioned specifications
controls.why: Spec-driven work needs specifications that are reviewed and versioned like code.
controls.remediation: Keep specifications under specs/ or docs/specs/ in the repository.

controls.label: Executable acceptance scenarios
controls.why: Acceptance has to be executable for an evaluator to be independent of the implementer.
controls.remediation: Express acceptance scenarios as executable tests (for example .feature files or an acceptance test suite).

controls.label: Independent evaluator
controls.why: The agent that implements a change must not be the only judge of it. Copilot code review, another AI reviewer, or a separate review, test or security agent all count.
controls.remediation: Turn on Copilot code review for pull requests, or define a separate review, test or security agent under .github/agents/.
controls.unknownReason: Copilot code review turned on through a ruleset or organization policy leaves no file in the repository, so no evaluator found here does not mean there is none.
controls.detail: Not observable from the checked-out files alone.

controls.label: Agentic workflows
controls.why: Autonomy that runs on a schedule or an event has to be defined in the repository to be governed.
controls.remediation: Define agentic workflows in .github/workflows/ so their triggers and permissions are reviewable.
controls.detail: A GitHub-specific check, and this repository's remote is not on GitHub — not checked.

controls.label: Deployment environments declared
controls.why: Progressive delivery needs named environments before it can have gates.
controls.remediation: Declare `environment:` on the deploying job.
controls.unknownReason: Environments can be deployed to from a reusable workflow this scan cannot read.
controls.detail: A GitHub-specific check, and this repository's remote is not on GitHub — not checked.

controls.label: Environment protection rules
controls.why: A named environment without required reviewers or wait timers gates nothing.
controls.remediation: Add required reviewers or a wait timer to the production environment.
controls.detail: A GitHub-specific check, and this repository's remote is not on GitHub — not checked.

controls.label: Artifact attestations
controls.why: Once nobody reads every line, provenance is the evidence that the artefact you shipped is the one the governed pipeline built. It is a supply-chain control first, so it is recommended here rather than required.
controls.remediation: Use actions/attest-build-provenance in the release workflow.
controls.unknownReason: Attestations can be produced by workflows this scan cannot read, or by a shared reusable workflow.
controls.detail: A GitHub-specific check, and this repository's remote is not on GitHub — not checked.

controls.label: Documented risk classification
controls.why: Autonomy is permitted per risk class, so the risk classes have to exist and be written down.
controls.remediation: Classify the repository's change types by risk and state which classes may be handled autonomously.
controls.detail: A written policy or decision — not machine-detectable.
